text: The University of the Andes (Colombia) was founded in 1949 by Mario Laserna Pinzón as the first nonsectarian and non-politically affiliated university in Colombia. It began with 80 students and a small set of faculties, and has since grown into a large, interdisciplinary institution with 14 academic units. The university is autonomous and independent, fostering pluralism, diversity, dialogue, and academic excellence, with a mission to provide critical and ethical education to strengthen students' civic responsibilities. It is located in Bogotá's historical center and spans 180,551 square meters, featuring renovated industrial and religious buildings, laboratories, a central library, and sports facilities. The university's mascot, Seneca, is a goat symbolizing its founding era. It has a strong emphasis on international exchange, with over 119 partner universities in 34 countries. The student body is predominantly male (55%) and composed of top-performing high school students (95% from the top 1% nationally). The university's staff includes many PhD-holding faculty members, and its academic structure allows students to design personalized curricula across four cycles. Notable alumni include César Gaviria (former Colombian President), María Ángela Holguín (Minister of Foreign Affairs), and Ana María Rey (theoretical physicist).
